entities.name: ADAMTS13
observations: In murine renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), circulating and renal ADAMTS13 decrease; recombinant ADAMTS13 improves renal function, microvascular/endothelial function, inflammation, oxidative stress, and histologic injury.
A higher post-IRI plasma VWF:ADAMTS13 ratio correlates with oxidative stress and proteinuria in a chronic follow-up model.

entities.name: von Willebrand factor
observations: Renal IRI increases renal VWF expression and VWF dimers; VWF deficiency or function-blocking antibody improves renal blood flow, creatinine, tubular injury, and neutrophil infiltration.
Direct evidence for ultra-large VWF multimers and platelet-rich microthrombi in standard renal IRI remains limited.

entities.name: Kidney ischemia-reperfusion injury
observations: The ADAMTS13–VWF axis contributes to experimental renal IRI through endothelial injury, impaired renal microvascular perfusion, inflammation, oxidative stress, and tubular damage.
Evidence is predominantly preclinical; direct clinical evidence in isolated renal IRI is limited.

entities.name: ADAMTS13-VWF renal IRI involvement
observations: Multiple murine studies support a causal contribution of ADAMTS13–VWF imbalance to renal IRI, but do not definitively establish ULVWF-driven platelet-rich microthrombosis as the dominant mechanism.
